column1: # ZAP alert-rule dispositions for the nightly deep API scan
# Tab-separated, because that is what ZAP parses: <rule id><TAB><IGNORE |
# WARN | FAIL><TAB>(reason). A line separated by spaces is read as one field
# parses this file the way ZAP does and fails on a malformed line.
# EVERY LINE IS A NAMED RULE WITH A WRITTEN REASON, and the suite caps how many
# there may be. The alternative -- ZAP's `-I`, which passes every warning at
# once -- is forbidden: it is every suppression here, un-reviewed and unwritten,
# and it would silently absorb the next rule that starts firing.
# NOTHING MAY BE SUPPRESSED HERE FOR BEING INCONVENIENT. The passive header
# rules in particular stay armed on purpose: they are what turn
# backend/src/middleware/security_headers.py from an asserted control into a
# verified one, and they are the only thing that would notice the day a header
# stops being emitted at the edge. A test names five of them and fails if any

column3: (Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set - the scan target is a plain-http loopback instance; HSTS is emitted only when ENV is production or staging, see backend/src/middleware/security_headers.py, so over http this rule can only ever report the CI harness back to itself)

(Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments - reads HTML and JavaScript comments for developer notes; this API serves neither, and the rule's matches here are ordinary English words inside JSON error strings)

(Absence of Anti-CSRF Tokens - an HTML-form control, and a meaningless one for this API: every route authenticates from an Authorization header that a cross-site form cannot set, and no route accepts a cookie credential)
(Modern Web Application - informational, and it reports that a response looks like a JavaScript-driven page rather than a document; there are no pages here at all)
(Timestamp Disclosure - matches any epoch-shaped integer in a response body, and this API returns them as ordinary data: streak counts, week numbers and millisecond durations all trip it)
